# Erdős Problem 487

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/487](https://www.erdosproblems.com/487)
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [DaEr36] Davenport, H. and Erdős, P., *On sequences of positive integers*. Acta Arithmetica
  (1936), 147-151.
- [Kl71] Kleitman, Daniel, *Collections of subsets containing no two sets and their union*.
  Proceedings of the LA Meeting AMS (1971), 153-155.
-/

namespace Erdos487

/--
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ have positive density. Must there exist distinct $a,b,c\in A$ such
that $[a,b]=c$ (where $[a,b]$ is the least common multiple of $a$ and $b$)?

This is true, a consequence of the positive solution to [447] by Kleitman [Kl71].

Davenport and Erdős [DaEr36] showed that there must exist an infinite sequence $a_1<a_2\cdots$
in $A$ such that $a_i\mid a_j$ for all $i\leq j$, under the assumption that the upper logarithmic
density of $A$ is positive.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos487.lean"]
theorem erdos_487 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.HasPosDensity →
      ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, ∃ c ∈ A, a ≠ b ∧ b ≠ c ∧ a ≠ c ∧ Nat.lcm a b = c := by
  sorry

end Erdos487

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement requires one triple for each positive-density set, while [Er61], §II.1, also formulates the conclusion as infinitely many triples.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Deleting any finite initial segment preserves positive natural density. Apply the universally quantified Lean assertion to A \ {0,…,N} for every N to obtain triples arbitrarily far out, hence infinitely many triples. Conversely, infinitely many triples imply the existence of one. Both the arbitrarily-far and infinite-triple equivalences were proved independently of the sorry-backed problem theorem in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

reformulations.difference: The Lean sets may contain zero, whereas the original number-theoretic formulation concerns positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Removing zero preserves positive natural density, so the universally quantified versions with and without 0 ∉ A are equivalent. Moreover, Nat.lcm 0 b = 0 and Nat.lcm a 0 = 0 make zero incompatible with the required pairwise distinctness. The domain equivalence and witness positivity were checked in Lean.

review.notes: The sole declaration matches the website and [Er61] formulation. HasPosDensity requires an existing positive natural-density limit; [Er65b] and the linked proof additionally cover the stronger positive-lower-density version. Final Lean checks passed for finite/empty-set exclusion, satisfiable density hypotheses, small LCM cases, the reformulations, and the implication to the linked proof's [1,N] lower-density convention. The equivalence and density-bridge proofs have no sorryAx dependency. The source's affirmative PROVED (LEAN) status agrees with the metadata. Kleitman's 1971 full text was inaccessible; only its bibliographic records were obtained. The linked proof and its dependency were inspected for proof holes, but their original Lean 4.29.1 project was not rebuilt.
